points.t: Crops of **yellow pustules** fading to **brown ‘rusty’ dots** on palms and soles, or thick fissured plaques.
Neutrophilic inflammation (**IL-36 / IL-17**); **smoking** is the main modifiable trigger in PPP.
**Stop smoking**, very potent topical steroid (± occlusion), emollients; then specialist options.
**Generalised pustular psoriasis** (fever, sheets of pustules): emergency.

cause.lead: Two related conditions on the hands and feet.
points: **PPP**: chronic relapsing **sterile** pustules confined to palms and soles; now seen as **distinct from psoriasis** (not PSORS1/HLA-C*06), though 10–25% also have plaques.
PPP: adults 20–60, **women ≈ 4:1**, **70–90% current or ex-smokers** (nicotinic receptors on eccrine ducts).
PPP links: thyroid disease, coeliac, diabetes, psoriatic arthritis, SAPHO; can be triggered by **TNF-α inhibitors**.
**Palmoplantar psoriasis**: Koebner from friction or manual work, infection, stress, lithium, β-blockers, alcohol, obesity.

visuals.caption: A sterile pustule (left) dries yellow-brown (middle) and leaves a flat rusty-brown macule with peeling scale (right). Pustules, brown dots and scale side by side are the PPP signature.
visuals.alt: Three stages from pustule to brown macule

features.lead: Pustules and brown dots, or sharp-edged thick plaques.
points: PPP: crops of **1–10 mm yellow pustules** on thenar and hypothenar eminences, central palms, insteps, heels.
Pustules dry to **brown ‘rusty’ macules**; scale and fissures; **burning or pain > itch**; symmetrical.
Palmoplantar psoriasis: well-defined red scaly plaques, or diffuse thick hyperkeratosis with little redness.
Painful **fissures**, sharp border; more **nail psoriasis** and **psoriatic arthritis**: screen with PEST.

visuals.caption: Typical PPP sites: the thenar and hypothenar eminences of the palm, the instep and the heel. Fingers and toes are usually spared.
visuals.alt: Palm and sole with pustule clusters at thenar, hypothenar, instep and heel

items.name: Palm PPP
items.t: Pustules on thenar and central palm; culture sterile.

items.name: Sole PPP
items.t: Redness, scale, pustules and brown dots.

points: Pustules + brown dots on palms / soles, symmetrical.
Pustules are **sterile**: swab only to exclude infection.
Scrapings if **unilateral** or interdigital scale: exclude tinea.
PEST for psoriatic arthritis; thyroid / coeliac if symptomatic.

cards.name: Hyperkeratotic hand eczema
cards.clue: Hardest to separate; may need biopsy or patch tests; can coexist.

cards.name: Tinea pedis / manuum
cards.clue: Often one-sided; scale in creases; scrape.

cards.name: Pompholyx
cards.clue: Itchy deep ‘tapioca’ vesicles on finger sides.

cards.name: Generalised pustular psoriasis
cards.clue: Fever, sheets of pustules beyond hands and feet: emergency.

manage.lead: Smoking cessation and potent steroid first (NICE CG153 / CKS).

points: **Stop smoking**: the strongest modifiable factor; stop-smoking service / NRT.
Emollients; salicylic acid 2–5% or urea for scale.
**Very potent TCS** (clobetasol) ± overnight occlusion for PPP.
Psoriasis: potent / very potent TCS ± calcipotriol or combination product.
Apremilast and biologics per NICE psoriasis TAs; biologics less reliable in PPP.

limits.t: Pustules are sterile: antibiotics don’t help.

items.t: Fever with sheets of pustules beyond hands and feet: **generalised pustular psoriasis**.
Can’t work or walk: early dermatology referral.
Not responding to very potent steroid and smoking cessation.

pearls.t: Very potent steroid under cling film or cotton gloves at night, short periods, then step down.
Tell patients pustules are **sterile**: antibiotics won’t help.
Ask about joints (PEST) and chest-wall pain (SAPHO).

quiz.q: Single biggest modifiable factor in PPP?
quiz.a: Smoking: 70–90% are current or ex-smokers; stopping helps most.

quiz.q: Pustules on one foot with interdigital scale?
quiz.a: Scrape for tinea before labelling PPP.

quiz.q: Fever and sheets of pustules spreading off the hands?

quiz.a: Very potent topical steroid (e.g. clobetasol) ± overnight occlusion, plus emollient.
